transcript:
Meeting Header: 2026-02-20 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Jordan, Maya, Chris, Priya, Samir, Lena, Ben

[00:00] Jordan Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, with Maya our SE. Quick roll call?
[00:05] Chris Moreno: Hey Chris here — CTO at LumenHealth.
[00:08] Priya Kapoor: Priya, ML eng.
[00:10] Samir Desai: Samir, security.
[00:12] Lena Ortiz: Lena, product.
[00:14] Ben Yao: Ben, DevOps.
[00:16] Jordan Patel: Great. Objective for today is a focused model catalog demo — how you pick open models, what the benchmarks look like, and compatibility matrices for deploying on our hosted vs dedicated vs private. We'll also cover routing and fallback. Maya, kick us off?
[00:30] Maya Singh: Sure. I'll share my screen (screen shared). So first slide is the catalog — we curate open models and provide verified perf profiles. The key columns are model family, param count, tokenization type, fp/quantization profiles, recommended hardware and cost per token estimate.
[00:48] Priya Kapoor: Quick q — can you surface models that work well for long clinical notes? We're seeing a lot of 2k to 8k seq lengths.
[00:56] Maya Singh: Yeah we tag models for sequence length; for 4k+ we recommend the newer long-context variants — for example: Llama-3-8k, Mistral Long*, and some optimized LLama forks. Note, some names in the table are shortened so it might show as "Llama3-8k" or sometimes transcribed as "lama-three" in older exports, so just watch naming.
[01:20] Chris Moreno: And how reliable are the perf numbers — latency, throughput, cost?
[01:25] Maya Singh: The perf profiles are from our internal harness: microbenchmarks + representative prompt sets. We attach median p95 latencies for 256 and 1024 tokens, and throughput at given batch sizes. There's also a compatibility matrix that flags if a model supports INT8/4 quant, KV cache behavior, and whether we have optimized kernels for A100/RTX/TSM. Important caveat: models vary by tokenizer; cost per token is an estimate.
[01:51] Priya Kapoor: Is INT8 always supported? We want to keep quality for clinical accuracy.
[01:55] Maya Singh: Not always. The matrix shows support level: native FP16, INT8 with recommended quantization recipe, or experimental INT4. We recommend running a small eval set — our Optimize tool can run quality regressions and surface metric delta after quantizing. That helps you pick a quant profile that hits your latency/cost target without dropping ROUGE or hallucination rates beyond your threshold.
[02:20] Samir Desai: From security, we need to confirm KMS integration and that keys never leave customer control on Private deployments. Also audit logs and retention controls.
[02:30] Jordan Patel: Yes, for Redwood Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM, keys stay in your vault. Audit logs are available with per-request metadata, and Console exposes per-route tracing. We'll attach SOC2 + ISO docs.
[02:44] Ben Yao: For on-prem or VPC, what about necessary hardware/AMI images? We run on GCE and Azure primarily.
[02:52] Maya Singh: We support both. The compatibility matrix includes kernel packs for CUDA 11/12 and ROCm where available; for Azure/GCP we supply deployment manifests. For dedicated pools, we can suggest instance families (e.g., A100-80GB for large context, H100 for throughput) and expected tokens/sec for a given batch profile.
[03:15] Lena Ortiz: Can you show an example selection flow? How would you choose model X vs Y for summarization?
[03:20] Maya Singh: Yeah demo mode. (screen) Start with your requirement tags: task=clinical-summarization, max_seq=8k, desired latency p95 < 600ms for 256 tokens, cost target <$0.002/token. Filter the catalog, then sort by quality metric (we surface a composite eval score from evals run on representative datasets). Then cross-check compatibility column for INT8 support and whether we have a verified optimized kernel for your hardware.
[03:52] Priya Kapoor: That composite eval score — is it specific to our domain?
[03:56] Maya Singh: We ship general eval sets; however, you can upload custom prompt sets into Optimize and run regression tests. That's what we'd recommend — upload 100-500 representative prompts and we'll run side-by-side comparisons across model variants and quant profiles.
[04:15] Chris Moreno: About fallback — if a model variant is out of capacity, can we route to a cheaper variant?
[04:20] Jordan Patel: Yes. Smart routing allows policy-based routing by latency/cost/region. You can set tiers — primary (higher perf) and fallback (cheaper quantized) with automatic retry and signal-based degradation. For strict SLA, we do canary strategies too.
[04:38] Ben Yao: Any known gotchas with KV cache and long context when using quantized weights?
[04:42] Maya Singh: Some experimental INT4 pipelines can have KV precision issues for very long context; our matrix flags which models had KV regressions in our internal tests. We generally recommend INT8 for long context production.
[05:00] Priya Kapoor: Can we run a benchmark with our own prompts and see p95 and token cost?
[05:04] Maya Singh: Absolutely. We'll provision a sandbox with sample data and credentials. We'll run the Optimize runner to output p50/p95, tokens/sec, and per-token cost breakdown.
[05:18] Chris Moreno: On the legal side, any issues with open models and weights? We need to ensure license compatibility for commercial use.
[05:25] Jordan Patel: We annotate license type in the catalog (MIT, Apache, permissive, or restricted). We can provide a vendor risk note but you should have legal review. For models with unclear licensing we flag them as "review required".
[05:44] Priya Kapoor: How granular is the Console for per-route cost breakdown? We need to attribute spend per team/product.
[05:50] Maya Singh: Console shows token-level cost per API key or route, with breakdown by model variant and quant profile. You can export CSVs and integrate with BigQuery via our export connector.
[06:05] Lena Ortiz: Any real customer benchmarks you can share for similar healthcare workloads?
[06:10] Maya Singh: We have a benchmark sheet for a hospital summarization workload — p95s and costs for Llama-3-8k, Mistral-7B-Long, and one optimized 13B variant. I'll share the Google Sheet link after the call. (link: redwood-benchmarks.example/reports)
[06:28] Chris Moreno: Great. Priya — can you outline the prompts you'll share?
[06:32] Priya Kapoor: Will do, probably 200 prompts focusing on discharge summaries and radiology notes, plus desired extraction fields.
[06:40] Jordan Patel: Cool. Quick demo of the compatibility matrix screen — shows columns: tokenizer mismatch, quant support, kernel status (verified/experimental), KV cache behavior, expected memory. You can click into a model to see exact kernel versions and the quant recipe we used.
[07:00] Samir Desai: For enterprise we need SSO and RBAC controls too.
[07:04] Maya Singh: We support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and role-based policies. For Private installs you can integrate with your internal IdP.
[07:14] Ben Yao: Any limitation on batch sizes for low latency? We want per-request latency < 400ms.
[07:20] Maya Singh: Low-latency shapes favor batch size=1 with small micro-batching. Our runtime uses continuous batching but you can tune thresholds. For p95 <400ms it's model/hardware dependent; we'll run bench with your prompts.
[07:36] (ambient typing and short pause)
[07:45] Jordan Patel: Let's talk pilot scope — recommended path: 1) provision sandbox, 2) run Optimize evals with your prompts across 3 candidate models and quant profiles, 3) pick runway model and scale to dedicated pool if needed. Does that align?
[08:00] Chris Moreno: Sounds good. Timeline — we'd like results in 2 weeks.
[08:04] Jordan Patel: We'll aim for 10 business days. Maya will own running the bench.
[08:12] Priya Kapoor: One more — can we pin model versions and freeze rollout? We need predictable outputs for regulatory validation.
[08:18] Maya Singh: Yes, you can pin model versions and also lock quantization profiles in a rollout policy. We support canary, A/B, and automatic rollback on quality regressions.
[08:33] Samir Desai: Please add retention controls for logs and audit exports; we need 7 years of audit for some pieces.
[08:40] Jordan Patel: We'll include retention config options in the docs. Samir, expect SOC2 and retention examples in the follow-up.
[08:50] (screen share ends)
[09:00] Jordan Patel: Recap and next steps: Jordan share model catalog CSV + benchmarks; Maya provision sandbox and run initial 3-model bench; Priya provide prompt sets; Samir send compliance questions. Any other blockers?
[09:18] Lena Ortiz: No blockers from product side.
[09:21] Ben Yao: I'll coordinate infra networking with Maya.
[09:24] Chris Moreno: We're good. Thanks everyone.
[09:27] Jordan Patel: Thanks — we'll follow up with links and invites.

Transcript notes: occasional mis-heard product names (e.g., "Llama" transcribed as "lama"), some overlap in speakers when multiple people react quickly.
